2) Core deep validation behavior: - Requirement parsing from story files: - Function loadAndCacheRequirements(...) reads the referenced story file with `fs.readFileSync(resolvedStoryPath, "utf8")`, uses regex `/REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g` to find requirement IDs, and stores them in a `Map<string, Set>` cache (implements REQ-DEEP-PARSE and REQ-DEEP-CACHE). - Matching `@req` annotations to story content: - extractReqIdFromLine(line) splits `@req` lines to get the requirement ID. - resolveStoryAndRequirements(...) calls validateAndResolveStoryPath(...) then loadAndCacheRequirements(...) to obtain the Set of IDs for the story. - checkRequirementExists(...) verifies `reqSet.has(reqId)` and reports via ESLint if missing (implements REQ-DEEP-MATCH and REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - Path validation and resolution: - validateAndResolveStoryPath({ comment, context, storyPath, cwd }) rejects paths containing `..` or absolute paths (via `path.isAbsolute`), and ensures the resolved path stays within `cwd`. On failure it reports `messageId: "invalidPath"` with the problematic `storyPath` (implements REQ-DEEP-PATH and contributes to error handling and UX). - Comment/annotation processing integration: - extractStoryPath(comment) scans comment lines for `@story` and extracts the story path. - handleAnnotationLine(...) routes lines starting with `@story`, `@req`, and `@implements` to the appropriate validators, updating or using the active `storyPath`. - processCommentLines(...) and processAllComments(...) walk all comments from `context.getSourceCode().getAllComments()`, ensuring every annotation in the file participates in deep validation. - programListener(context) initializes `reqCache` and returns a Program visitor, wiring this logic into ESLint’s normal lifecycle.

6) Documentation of deep validation behavior: - File: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md - Story linkage and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Parse story files to extract requirement identifiers` - `@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH - Validate @req references against story file content` - `@req REQ-DEEP-PATH - Protect against path traversal in story paths` - Describes behavior in line with the story: - Parses referenced story files to extract requirement IDs (REQ-XXX-YYY). - Ensures each `@req` / `@implements` ID exists in the story. - Reports `invalidPath` for traversal/absolute paths. - Reports `reqMissing` when a requirement is not found. - Explains requirement IDs are scoped per story file and may repeat across stories. - Provides multiple, concrete examples (correct and incorrect) covering `@story`+`@req`, `@implements`, and path issues, fulfilling the Documentation acceptance criterion.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied. The `valid-req-reference` rule parses story files, caches discovered requirement IDs, and validates that every `@req` (and, via related story 010.2, `@implements`) annotation points to a requirement that truly exists in the referenced story file. It integrates with the existing plugin architecture, provides clear and specific error messages (`reqMissing`, `invalidPath`), handles different markdown formats and structures via a robust regex-based scan and dedicated fixtures, gracefully handles unreadable/malformed story files, and is documented with rule-level docs and worked examples. Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts explicitly reference this story and assert both successful and failing deep-validation scenarios. Therefore, this story’s implementation is complete and passes the specified requirements.
